newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa maize harvest seen in full swing end-May.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa maize harvest seen in full swing end-May.

text.p: South Africa's 1997 maize harvest will kick into full swing by the end of May but early indications are that the crop will be almost two million tonnes less than last year, the National Maize Producers Organisation (NAMPO) said on Friday.
NAMPO economist Andre Ferreira said farmers were only due to begin harvesting at the end of the month.
"The harvest hasn't really started, some farmers have started but large-scale harvesting will only start towards the end of the month," Ferreira told Reuters.
The last official estimate by the country's National Crop Estimates committee set the 1997 maize crop at 7.66 million tonnes -- sharply down from the 9.694 million in 1996.
Ferreira said the committee will give its new crop estimate on May 20.
"We will get a better idea of the size of the crop next week, I don't think it will change much," Ferreira said.

This year's crop was expected to deliver 4.109 million tonnes of white maize and 3.551 million tonnes of yellow compared to 1996's 5.836 million tonnes of white maize and 3.858 million tonnes of yellow.
The committee said in March that the main culprit for the reduced crop was dry weather in the major maize-growing areas of the North West province and western Free State.
The 1997 crop estimate is around one million tonnes above average consumption which is between six and 6-1/2 million tonnes.
Industry officials said the reduced crop would result in sharply lower export earnings at a time when the South African maize industry is deregulated for the first time time in 60 years.
The state-owned Maize Board is currently being wound up and since the start of the new season on May 1, private traders have been free to export as much maize as they want.
Previously the government set export limits but legislation tabled last year abolished all controls on South Africa's maize market.
